title.zh: 卷十七 志第九 輿服
title.raw: 卷十七 志第九 輿服 Volume 17 Treatises 9: Caraiges and Dress

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷十七‧志第九

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 17 — Treatise 9
translations.idiomatic: Volume 17 Treatises 9: Carriages and Dress

sentences.zh: 昔三皇乘祇車出谷口，夏氏以奚仲爲車正，殷有瑞車，山車垂句是也。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Three Sovereigns rode the spirit carriage out from the valley mouth; the Xia made Xi Zhong Master of Chariots; the Yin had the auspicious carriage — the mountain carriage with drooping axles is meant.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Three Sovereigns rode the sacred carriage out from the valley gate; the Xia appointed Xi Zhong Master of Chariots; the Yin had the auspicious chariot — the mountain cart with drooping axles tells that tale.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》匠人爲輿，以象天地。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou the craftsman builds the carriage to symbolize Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou have the craftsman shape the carriage as Heaven and Earth in miniature.

sentences.zh: 漢武天漢四年，朝諸侯甘泉宮，定輿服制，班于天下。

translations.literal: In Tianhan year 4 of Han Wudi, he convened the feudal lords at Sweet Springs Palace, fixed the carriage-and-dress code, and promulgated it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In Han Wudi's Tianhan 4 he assembled the feudal lords at Sweet Springs Palace, set the carriage and regalia code, and sent it throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 光武建武十三年，得公孫述葆車，輿輦始具。

translations.literal: In Jianwu year 13 Guangwu obtained Gongsun Shu's treasure carriage; litters and palanquins were first complete.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangwu's Jianwu 13 he captured Gongsun Shu's treasure carriage; the full set of state litters was first assembled.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕創立此志，馬彪勒成漢典，晉摯虞治禮，亦議五輅制度。

translations.literal: Cai Yong founded this treatise; Ma Biao compiled the Han canon; Jin's Zhi Yu curated the rites and likewise debated the system of the Five Regalia Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong began this treatise; Ma Biao finished the Han record; under Jin, Zhi Yu curated the rites and debated the five ceremonial chariots as well.

sentences.zh: 江左之始，車服多闕，但有金戎，省充庭之儀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the southeastern court, carriages and dress were largely lacking; only the golden war carriage remained, and the hall-filling ceremony was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the southeast court, carriages and dress were mostly missing; only the golden war carriage survived, and the palace-yard display was cut back.

sentences.zh: 太興中，太子臨學，無高蓋車，元帝詔乘安車。

translations.literal: In the Taixing era, when the crown prince attended school there was no high-canopy carriage; Emperor Yuan decreed that he ride the comfort carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixing, when the crown prince went to his studies there was no high-canopy coach; Yuan Di decreed he use the comfort carriage instead.

sentences.zh: 元、明時，屬車唯九乘。

translations.literal: In the Yuan and Ming reigns, the following carriages numbered only nine.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Yuan and Ming, the train had only nine following carriages.

sentences.zh: 永和中，石虎死後，舊工人奔叛歸國，稍造車輿。

translations.literal: In the Yonghe era, after Shi Hu's death, veteran craftsmen deserted and returned to the state; chariots were gradually made again.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe, after Shi Hu died, old artisans fled home and chariot-making slowly resumed.

sentences.zh: 太元中，苻堅敗後，又得偽車輦，於是屬車增爲十二乘。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era, after Fu Jian's defeat, they again obtained the Former Qin litters; then the following carriages increased to twelve.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan, after Fu Jian's defeat they seized Former Qin litters and raised the train to twelve carriages.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，宋武平關、洛，得姚興偽車輦。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era Song Wu pacified the Pass and Luoyang and obtained Yao Xing's Former Qin litters.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi, Emperor Wu of Song took the Pass and Luoyang and captured Yao Xing's Qin litters.

sentences.zh: 宋大明改脩輦輅，妙盡時華，始備偽氐，復設充庭之制。

translations.literal: In Song's Daming era they renovated the litters and regalia chariots, exhaustingly refined in contemporary splendor; they first completed the Qin set and restored the hall-filling institution.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song's Daming they rebuilt the litters and ceremonial chariots with every luxury of the age, first completed the Qin equipment, and restored the palace-yard display.

sentences.zh: 永明中，更增藻飾，盛於前矣。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era they further added ornamental refinement, surpassing what came before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming they added still richer ornament — grander than ever.

sentences.zh: 案《周禮》以檢《漢志》，名器不同，晉、宋改革，稍與世異，今記時事而已。

translations.literal: Checking the Rites of Zhou against the Han Treatise, the names and vessels differ; Jin and Song reforms diverged somewhat from the age; this record sets down present affairs only.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the Rites of Zhou and the Han Treatise, titles and regalia no longer match; Jin and Song revisions drifted from ancient usage — here only the present is recorded.

sentences.zh: 玉輅，漢金根也。

translations.literal: The jade regalia carriage was the Han golden-root carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Regalia Chariot was the Han "golden-root" carriage.

sentences.zh: 漆畫輪，金塗縱容後路受福輠。

translations.literal: Lacquered and painted wheels; gold-plated longitudinal rails, rear track, and "Receiving Blessing" wheel spokes.
translations.idiomatic: Lacquer-painted wheels; gold-plated longitudinal rails, rear track, and "Receiving Blessing" spokes.

sentences.zh: 兩廂上望板前優遊，通緣金塗鏤鍱，碧絞罽，鑿鏤金薄帖。

translations.literal: On both side panels, before the viewing board, the "Leisurely Tour" rail; continuous borders of gold-plated openwork plaques, green twisted gauze and felt, and chased gold foil appliqué.
translations.idiomatic: On both side panels, before the viewing board, the "Leisurely Tour" rail; gold openwork borders, green twisted gauze and felt, and chased gold foil.

sentences.zh: 兩廂外織成衣，兩廂裏上施金塗鏤面釘，瑇瑁帖。

translations.literal: Outside both side panels, brocade-woven garments; inside both side panels above, gold-plated openwork face-nails and tortoiseshell appliqué.
translations.idiomatic: Outside both panels, brocade-woven covers; inside both panels above, gold openwork face-nails and tortoiseshell inlay.

sentences.zh: 望板廂上金薄帖，金博山，登仙紐，松精。

translations.literal: On the viewing board and side panels, gold-foil appliqué, gold Mount Bo ornaments, "Ascending Immortal" clasps, and pine essence.
translations.idiomatic: On the viewing board and panels, gold foil, gold Mount Bo finials, "Ascending Immortal" clasps, and pine essence.

sentences.zh: 優遊上和鸞鳥立花趺銜鈴，銀帶瑇瑁筒瓦，金塗鏤鍱，刀格，織成手匡金花鈿錦衣。

translations.literal: Above the "Leisurely Tour" rail, phoenix birds standing on floral bases holding bells; silver bands, tortoiseshell tube tiles, gold-plated openwork plaques, blade-racks, brocade-woven hand-guards, golden-flower hairpins, and brocade garments.
translations.idiomatic: Above the "Leisurely Tour" rail, phoenixes on floral bases with bells; silver bands, tortoiseshell tube tiles, gold openwork plaques, blade-racks, brocade hand-guards, golden floral hairpins, and brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 優遊下，隱膝，裏施金塗鏤面釘，織成文。

translations.literal: Below the "Leisurely Tour" rail, knee screens; inside, gold-plated openwork face-nails and brocade patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Below the "Leisurely Tour" rail, knee screens lined with gold openwork face-nails and brocade.

sentences.zh: 優遊橫前，施瑇瑁帖，金塗花釘。

translations.literal: Before the "Leisurely Tour" cross-rail, tortoiseshell appliqué and gold-plated floral nails.
translations.idiomatic: Before the "Leisurely Tour" cross-rail, tortoiseshell inlay and gold floral nails.

sentences.zh: 優遊前，金塗倒龍，後梢鑿銀瑇瑁龜甲，金塗花沓。

translations.literal: Before the "Leisurely Tour" rail, gold-plated inverted dragons; behind the tip, chased silver tortoiseshell tortoise-shell pattern and gold-plated floral tiers.
translations.idiomatic: Before the "Leisurely Tour" rail, gold inverted dragons; on the rear tip, chased silver tortoiseshell scalework and gold floral tiers.

sentences.zh: 望板，金塗受福望龍諸校飾。

translations.literal: On the viewing board, gold-plated "Receiving Blessing" viewing dragons and other ornamental fittings.
translations.idiomatic: On the viewing board, gold "Receiving Blessing" viewing dragons and other trim.

sentences.zh: 抗及諸末，皆螭龍首。

translations.literal: The shafts and all terminal fittings were dragon-headed.
translations.idiomatic: Shafts and every end-piece bore dragon heads.

sentences.zh: 龍汗板，在車前，銀帶花獸，金塗受福，緣裏邊，鏤鍱瑇瑁織成衣。

translations.literal: The dragon-sweat board, before the carriage, with silver bands and floral beasts, gold-plated "Receiving Blessing," bordered inside, openwork plaques, tortoiseshell, and brocade-woven garments.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon-sweat board before the carriage: silver bands and floral beasts, gold "Receiving Blessing," bordered lining, openwork plaques, tortoiseshell, and brocade covers.

sentences.zh: 裏，金塗鏤面花釘。

translations.literal: Inside, gold-plated openwork floral nails.
translations.idiomatic: Inside, gold openwork floral nails.

sentences.zh: 外，金塗博山、辟邪虎、鳳皇銜花諸校飾。

translations.literal: Outside, gold-plated Mount Bo, demon-quelling tigers, phoenixes holding flowers, and other ornamental fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Outside, gold Mount Bo finials, demon-quelling tigers, flower-bearing phoenixes, and other trim.

sentences.zh: 斗蓋，金塗鏤鍱，二十八爪支子花，黃錦斗衣，復碧絹染布緣油頂，絳系絡，織成顏芚赭舌孔雀毛復錦，綠絞隨陰，懸珠蚌佩，金塗鈴，雲朱結，仙人綬，雜色真孔雀毦。

translations.literal: The canopy: gold-plated openwork plaques; twenty-eight clawed branch-and-flower supports; yellow brocade canopy garments; again green silk dyed border-cloth on the oiled top; crimson cords and nettings; brocade with red ochre tongue, peacock feathers, and layered brocade; green twisted gauze following the shade; suspended pearl and clam pendants; gold-plated bells; cloud-cinnabar knots; immortal sashes; and mixed true peacock down.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy: gold openwork plaques; twenty-eight clawed floral struts; yellow brocade canopy cloth; green dyed border-silk on the oiled crown; crimson cords and netting; brocade with red ochre tongue, peacock feather, and layered brocade; green twisted gauze shading; pearl and clam pendants; gold bells; cloud-cinnabar knots; immortal sashes; and mixed peacock down.

sentences.zh: 一轅，漆畫車衡，銀花帶，衡上金塗博山，四和鸞鳥立花趺銜鈴，所謂「鸞鳥立衡」也。

translations.literal: One shaft; lacquered and painted axle-tree; silver floral bands; on the axle-tree a gold-plated Mount Bo; on four harmonizing phoenix birds standing on floral bases holding bells — what is called 「phoenix birds standing on the axle-tree」.
translations.idiomatic: One shaft; lacquer-painted axle-tree; silver floral bands; on the axle-tree a gold Mount Bo; four harmonizing phoenixes on floral bases with bells — the so-called 「phoenixes standing on the axle-tree」.

sentences.zh: 又龍首銜軛，叉髦插翟尾，上下花沓，絳綠系的，望繩八枚。

translations.literal: Again a dragon head holding the yoke; forked plumes inserting pheasant tails; floral tiers above and below; crimson and green cords; eight viewing ropes.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon head on the yoke; forked plumes set with pheasant tails; floral tiers above and below; crimson and green cords; eight viewing ropes.

sentences.zh: 旂十二旒，畫升龍，竿首金塗龍銜火燄幡，真毦。

translations.literal: The banner with twelve pendants, painted ascending dragons; at the pole top a gold-plated dragon holding a flame pennant; true down.
translations.idiomatic: A twelve-tasseled banner painted with ascending dragons; at the pole top a gold dragon holding a flame pennant; true down trim.

sentences.zh: 棨戟，織成衣，金塗沓駐及受福，金塗鴈鏤鍱。

translations.literal: Ceremonial halberds with brocade-woven garments, gold-plated tiered rests and "Receiving Blessing," and gold-plated goose openwork plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial halberds in brocade covers, gold tiered rests and "Receiving Blessing," and gold goose openwork plaques.

sentences.zh: 漆案立牀，在車中，錦復黃絞，爲案立衣。

translations.literal: A lacquered case standing as a bed, within the carriage; yellow twisted gauze with brocade backing, serving as the case-standing garment.
translations.idiomatic: A lacquered standing case-bed inside the carriage; brocade-backed yellow twisted gauze as its cover.

sentences.zh: 錦復黃絞鄣泥。

translations.literal: Brocade-backed yellow twisted gauze mud-guards.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade-backed yellow twisted gauze wheel mud-guards.

sentences.zh: 八幅，長九尺，緣紅錦芚帶，織成花芚的。

translations.literal: Eight panels, nine feet long, with red brocade tongue-bands on the border and brocade-woven floral tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Eight panels nine feet long, red brocade tongue-bands on the borders, and brocade floral tongues.

sentences.zh: 五輅，江左相承駕四馬，左右騑爲六。

translations.literal: The Five Regalia Chariots: south of the Yangtze they successively used four horses to draw them, with left and right outriders making six.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Regalia Chariots: in the southeast court they were routinely drawn by four horses, with left and right outriders making six in all.

sentences.zh: 施絳系游御繩，其重轂貳轄飛軨幡，用赤油令，有紫真毦。

translations.literal: Crimson cord touring reins were fitted; their double hubs, paired linchpins, flying naves, and pennants used the red-oil decree, with purple true down.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson touring reins were fitted; double hubs, paired linchpins, flying nave pennants followed the red-oil rule, with purple true down.

sentences.zh: 左纛，置左騑馬軛上。

translations.literal: The left great banner was set on the yoke of the left outrider horse.
translations.idiomatic: The left great banner was fixed to the left outrider's yoke.

sentences.zh: 金鍐，金加冠，狀如玉華形，在馬鍐上。

translations.literal: The golden cheek-piece — gold added to the crown, shaped like the jade-flower form, set on the horse's cheek-piece.
translations.idiomatic: The golden cheek-piece: gold crowned in a jade-flower shape, mounted on the horse's cheek-piece.

sentences.zh: 方釳，鐵廣數寸，有三孔，插翟尾其中。

translations.literal: The square iron plate, several inches wide, with three holes for inserting pheasant tails.
translations.idiomatic: The square iron plate, several inches across, with three holes to take pheasant tails.

sentences.zh: 繁纓，金塗紫皮，紫真毦，橫在馬膺前。

translations.literal: The full tassel-crown: gold-plated purple leather and purple true down, set crosswise before the horse's breast.
translations.idiomatic: The full tassel-crown: gold-plated purple leather and purple true down, laid crosswise before the horse's breast.

sentences.zh: 鏤鍚，刻金爲馬面當顱。

translations.literal: The carved golden brow: gold chased as the horse's forehead plate.
translations.idiomatic: The carved golden brow: gold chased into the horse's forehead plate.

sentences.zh: 皆如古制。

translations.literal: All followed the ancient institution.
translations.idiomatic: All followed the ancient pattern.

sentences.zh: 世祖永明初，加玉輅爲重蓋，又作麒麟頭，采畫，以馬首戴之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming, Emperor Shizu added a double canopy to the jade regalia carriage and also made a qilin head, painted in colors, to be worn on the horse's head.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming, Emperor Shizu gave the Jade Regalia Chariot a double canopy and fashioned a painted qilin head for the horses to wear.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良啓曰：「臣聞車旗有章，載自前史，器必依禮，服無舛法。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling submitted: 「I have heard that carriage banners have their regulations, recorded from former histories; vessels must follow ritual, and dress must not violate law.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling submitted: 「I have heard that carriage banners have their statutes, set down in earlier histories; regalia must follow ritual, and dress must not break the code.

sentences.zh: 凡蓋員象天，軫方法地，上無二天之儀，下設兩蓋之飾，求之志錄，恐爲乖衷。

translations.literal: The canopy is round to symbolize Heaven; the naves square to symbolize Earth. Above there is no rite of two Heavens; below you set the ornament of two canopies — sought in the ritual records, I fear this is contrary to the intent.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy is round as Heaven; the naves square as Earth. Above there is no rite of two heavens; below you add a double-canopy ornament — checked against the ritual records, I fear it misses the mark.

sentences.zh: 又假爲麟首，加乎馬頭，事不師古，鮮或可施。

translations.literal: Again you falsely make a qilin head and set it on the horse's head; the matter does not take the ancients as teacher — scarcely can it be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Again you set a false qilin head on the horses; the thing does not follow antiquity — it can hardly be allowed.

sentences.zh: 」建武中，明帝乃省重蓋等。

translations.literal: 」In the Jianwu era, Emperor Ming then abolished the double canopy and the like.
translations.idiomatic: 」In the Jianwu era, Emperor Ming abolished the double canopy and similar additions.

sentences.zh: 金輅。

translations.literal: Gold chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Gold chariot.

sentences.zh: 制度校飾如玉輅，而稍減少，亦以金塗。

translations.literal: Regulations and trim ornamentation like the jade chariot, but somewhat reduced; also gilt.
translations.idiomatic: Its fittings followed the jade chariot’s pattern, somewhat pared back, and were gilt throughout.

sentences.zh: 象輅。

translations.literal: Ivory chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory chariot.

sentences.zh: 如金輅而制飾又減。

translations.literal: Like the gold chariot, but regulation ornamentation further reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Like the gold chariot, with still plainer regulated trim.

sentences.zh: 木輅。

translations.literal: Wood chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Wood chariot.

sentences.zh: 制飾如象輅而尤減。

translations.literal: Regulation ornamentation like the ivory chariot but reduced still more.
translations.idiomatic: Regulated trim like the ivory chariot’s, reduced yet further.

sentences.zh: 革輅，如大輅。

translations.literal: Leather chariot, like the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Leather chariot, patterned on the great chariot.

sentences.zh: 建大麾。

translations.literal: It raises a great banner.
translations.idiomatic: It bore a great command banner.

sentences.zh: 赤旗也。

translations.literal: A red flag.
translations.idiomatic: A red banner.

sentences.zh: 首施火燄幡。

translations.literal: At the pole-top a flame pennant is affixed.
translations.idiomatic: The polehead carried a flame pennant.

sentences.zh: 宋昇明三年，錫齊王大輅、戎輅各一。

translations.literal: In Shengming year 3 of Song, one great chariot and one war chariot each were bestowed on the King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Shengming 3 the court bestowed on the King of Qi one great chariot and one war chariot.

sentences.zh: 乘黃五輅，無大輅、戎輅。

translations.literal: The five chariots under the Director of Carriages had no great chariot or war chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Carriages’ five chariots included no great chariot or war chariot.

sentences.zh: 左丞王逡之議：「大輅，殷之祭車，故不登周輅之名，而《明堂位》云『大輅，殷輅也』。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Grandee Wang Xunzhi argued: 「The great chariot was Yin’s sacrificial carriage; therefore it does not appear among the Zhou chariot names. Yet the Hall of Brightness says 『The great chariot is the Yin chariot.』
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Grandee Wang Xunzhi argued: 「The great chariot was Yin’s sacrificial carriage, which is why it is absent from the Zhou chariot roster—yet the Hall of Brightness states, 『The great chariot is the Yin chariot.』

sentences.zh: 注云『大輅，木輅也』。

translations.literal: The comment says 『The great chariot is the wood chariot.』
translations.idiomatic: The commentary reads: 『The great chariot is the wood chariot.』

sentences.zh: 《月令》『中央土，乘大輅』。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances: 『In the center, earth—ride the great chariot.』
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances: 『At the center, earth—ride the great chariot.』

sentences.zh: 注云『殷輅也』。

translations.literal: The comment says 『The Yin chariot.』
translations.idiomatic: The commentary: 『The Yin chariot.』

sentences.zh: 《禮器》『大輅繁纓一就』。

translations.literal: Ritual Vessels: 『The great chariot—plaited tassels, one set.』
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Vessels: 『The great chariot—plaited tassels in one set.』

sentences.zh: 注云『大輅，殷之祭天車也』。

translations.literal: The comment says 『The great chariot is Yin’s carriage for sacrificing to Heaven.』
translations.idiomatic: The commentary: 『The great chariot is Yin’s carriage for sacrificing to Heaven.』

sentences.zh: 《周禮》五路，玉路、金路、象路、革路、木路。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou lists five paths: jade path, gold path, ivory path, leather path, and wood path.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou names five paths: jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood.

sentences.zh: 則周之木輅，殷之大路也。

translations.literal: Thus Zhou’s wood chariot is Yin’s great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou’s wood chariot, then, is Yin’s great chariot.

sentences.zh: 周革路建大白，以卽戎，此則戎路也。

translations.literal: Zhou’s leather path raises the great white [banner] to go to war—this is the war path.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou’s leather path raises the great white standard for war—this is the war path.

sentences.zh: 意謂國之大事，在祀與戎，故錫以殷祭天之車，與周之卽戎之路。

translations.literal: The reasoning is that the great affairs of state lie in sacrifice and war; therefore they were granted Yin’s Heaven-sacrificing carriage and Zhou’s war-going path.
translations.idiomatic: The point is that a state’s weightiest business is sacrifice and war—hence the grant of Yin’s Heaven-sacrificing carriage together with Zhou’s war chariot.

sentences.zh: 祀則以殷，戎必以周者，明郊天義遠，建前代之禮，卽戎事近，故以今世之制。

translations.literal: For sacrifice use Yin; for war necessarily use Zhou—showing that suburban Heaven rites are remote in meaning and establish a prior age’s ritual, while military matters are near, so the present dynasty’s regulation applies.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice follows Yin; war must follow Zhou—because suburban Heaven worship looks far back and installs an earlier dynasty’s rite, whereas military affairs are immediate and call for the current house’s forms.

sentences.zh: 《明堂位》云『魯君孟春乘大路，載十有二旒日月之章，祀帝于郊』。

translations.literal: The Hall of Brightness says 『In mid-spring the lord of Lu rides the great road [chariot], bearing twelve streamers with sun-and-moon emblems, sacrificing to the Thearch in the suburbs.』
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Brightness says: 『In mid-spring the lord of Lu rides the great road chariot, with twelve sun-and-moon streamers, and sacrifices to the Thearch in the suburbs.』

sentences.zh: 天必以大輅以錫諸侯，良有以也。

translations.literal: That Heaven must bestow the great chariot upon feudal lords is well founded indeed.
translations.idiomatic: That Heaven should bestow the great chariot on feudal lords is entirely reasonable.

sentences.zh: 今木路，卽大路也。

translations.literal: Now the wood path is precisely the great road [chariot].
translations.idiomatic: Today’s wood path is precisely that great road chariot.

sentences.zh: 」太尉左長史王儉議，宜用金輅九旒。

translations.literal: 」Grand Marshal’s left chief clerk Wang Jian argued that the gold chariot with nine streamers should be used.
translations.idiomatic: 」Grand Marshal’s left chief clerk Wang Jian proposed the gold chariot with nine streamers.

sentences.zh: 時乘黃無副，借用五輅，大朝臨軒，權列三輅。

translations.literal: At the time the Director of Carriages had no deputy; they borrowed the five chariots—for great court at the throne hall they provisionally arrayed three chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Carriages then had no deputy, so the five chariots were borrowed; at great court before the throne hall three chariots were set out provisionally.

sentences.zh: 玉、金輅，建碧旂。

translations.literal: Jade and gold chariots raise jade-green banners.
translations.idiomatic: The jade and gold chariots bore jade-green banners.

sentences.zh: 象、木輅，建赤旂。

translations.literal: Ivory and wood chariots raise red banners.
translations.idiomatic: The ivory and wood chariots bore red banners.

sentences.zh: 永明初，太子步兵校尉伏曼容議，以爲「齊德尚青，五路五牛及五色幡旗，竝宜以先青爲次。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongming, Palace Infantry Commandant Fu Manrong argued that 「Qi’s virtue honors green; the five paths, five oxen, and five-colored pennants and banners should all take green first in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming, Palace Infantry Commandant Fu Manrong argued: 「Qi’s virtue esteems green—the five paths, five oxen, and five-colored pennants and banners should all rank green first.

sentences.zh: 軍容戎事之所乘，犧牲繭握之所薦，竝宜悉依尚色。

translations.literal: What military display and war chariots ride, and what sacrificial victims and silk offerings present—all should wholly follow the honored color.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever war chariots and martial display require, and whatever victims and cocooned silk offerings demand, should all conform to the honored color.

sentences.zh: 三代服色，以姓音爲尚，漢不識音，故還尚其行運之色。

translations.literal: The three dynasties’ dress colors took clan pitch as their honor; Han did not understand pitch, so they reverted to honoring the color of their cycle of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dynasties set dress color by clan pitch-tone; Han lacked that science and fell back on the color of the reign’s element.

sentences.zh: 今旣無善律，則大齊所尚，亦宜依漢道。

translations.literal: Now that there is no skilled pitch-tube [expert], what Great Qi honors should likewise follow the Han way.
translations.idiomatic: With no master of the pitch tubes today, Great Qi’s honored color should likewise follow Han practice.

sentences.zh: 若有善吹律者，便應還取姓尚」。

translations.literal: If there were one skilled at blowing the tubes, then clan pitch should be taken up again.」
translations.idiomatic: Were a true pitch-tube master found, clan pitch could govern color once more.」

sentences.zh: 太子僕周顒議：「三代姓音，古無前記，裁音配尚，起自曼容。

translations.literal: Crown Prince’s Steward Zhou Yong argued: 「Clan pitch of the three dynasties has no ancient record; matching pitch to honored color began with Manrong.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince’s Steward Zhou Yong replied: 「No ancient record fixes the Three Dynasties’ clan pitch; pairing pitch to honored color starts with Manrong alone.

sentences.zh: 則是曼容善識姓聲，不復方假吹律。

translations.literal: Then Manrong is skilled at recognizing clan sounds and no longer needs to borrow tube-blowing at all.
translations.idiomatic: If so, Manrong already knows clan tones by ear and need not invoke pitch tubes at all.

sentences.zh: 何故能識遠代之宮商，而更迷皇朝之律呂，而云當今無知吹律以定所尚，宜附漢以從闕邪？

translations.literal: Why can he recognize remote ages’ gong and shang, yet be more confused about our dynasty’s lü and pitch-tubes, and say that today none can blow the tubes to fix what is honored—should we attach ourselves to Han to fill the gap?
translations.idiomatic: How can he discern the gong and shang of distant antiquity yet fumble our court’s pitch standards—and claim that because no one today can blow the tubes to fix the honored color, we should cling to Han out of convenience?

sentences.zh: 皇朝本以行運爲所尚，非關不定於音氏。

translations.literal: Our dynasty has always taken the cycle of fortune as what is honored; it is not that color cannot be fixed by clan pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Our house has always honored the reign’s element, not failed to settle color by clan pitch.

sentences.zh: 如此，設有善律之知音，不宜遵聲以爲尚。

translations.literal: On this showing, even if there were a pitch-master who knew sound, one should not follow tone as the honored [color].
translations.idiomatic: Even with a pitch-master who truly knew sound, tone should not dictate the honored color.

sentences.zh: 」散騎常侍劉朗之等十五人竝議駮之，事不行。

translations.literal: 」Fifteen including Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Langzhi all memorialized in rebuttal; the proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: 」Liu Langzhi, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and fourteen others jointly rebutted the proposal; it was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 皇太子象輅。

translations.literal: Crown Prince’s ivory chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince’s ivory chariot.

sentences.zh: 校飾如御，旂九旒降龍。

translations.literal: Trim ornamentation like the imperial [chariot]; banner nine streamers with descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Trim like the emperor’s carriage; a nine-streamer banner with descending dragons.

sentences.zh: 皇太后皇后重翟車，金塗校具，白地人馬錦帖，廂隱膝後戶，白牙的帖，金塗面釘，漆畫輪，鐵鐺，金塗縱容後路輠，師子轄，抗檐皆施金塗螭頭及神龍雀等諸飾。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager and Empress heavy-di carriage: gilt trim fittings; white-ground brocade appliqué on human and horse figures; side panels, hidden knee panels, and rear doors; white ivory appliqué; gilt face studs; lacquered painted wheels; iron hub caps; gilt zongrong rear-path fu-barrels; lion-shaped axle caps; crossbeams and eaves all bear gilt chi-dragon heads, spirit dragon-sparrows, and other ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager and Empress rode a heavy-di carriage with gilt fittings, brocade human and horse figures on a white ground, side panels with hidden knee screens and rear doors, white ivory appliqué, gilt face studs, lacquered wheels, iron hub caps, gilt rear axle housings, lion-shaped axle caps, and gilt chi-dragon heads, spirit dragon-sparrows, and the like on every crossbeam and canopy strut.

sentences.zh: 軛衡上施金博山，又有金塗長角巴首。

translations.literal: On the yoke and pole crossbar a gilt immortal mountain; also gilt long-horned ba heads.
translations.idiomatic: The yoke and pole crossbar bore a gilt Mount Bo and gilt long-horned ba heads.

sentences.zh: 蓋，金塗，爪支子花二十八，青油俠碧絹黃絞蓋，漆布裏。

translations.literal: Canopy: gilt, twenty-eight claw-and-branch flowers; green oil lining, layered jade-green silk and yellow brocade canopy, lacquered-cloth lining.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy was gilt with twenty-eight claw-and-branch flowers, lined in green oil, layered jade-green silk and yellow brocade, with a lacquered-cloth interior.

sentences.zh: 紫顏芚，黃絞紫絞隨陰，碧毛。

translations.literal: Purple-faced chen mats; yellow and purple brocade following shade; green plumes.
translations.idiomatic: Purple-faced chen mats; yellow and purple brocade by light and shade; green feather trim.

sentences.zh: 外上施絳紫系絡。

translations.literal: Outside above, crimson-purple cord netting is affixed.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson-purple cord netting hung above the exterior.

sentences.zh: 碧旂九旒，棨戟。

translations.literal: Jade-green banner, nine streamers; halberd-standards.
translations.idiomatic: A jade-green nine-streamer banner and halberd-standards.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉《東宮儀記》云中宮僕御重翟金根車，未詳得稱爲金根也。

translations.literal: The Yuanjia Eastern Palace Protocols of Song say the palace steward’s heavy-di golden-root carriage—it is unclear that it may be called golden-root.
translations.idiomatic: Song’s Yuanjia Eastern Palace Protocols mention the palace steward’s heavy-di golden-root carriage—whether it truly merited the name “golden-root” is unclear.

sentences.zh: 皇太子妃厭翟車。

translations.literal: The crown prince's consort [uses the] Yan Di carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort rode the Yan Di carriage.

sentences.zh: 如重翟，飾微減。

translations.literal: Like the heavy Yan Di [carriage], but ornament slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: It matched the heavy Yan Di carriage, with ornament somewhat reduced.

sentences.zh: 指南車。

translations.literal: South-pointing carriage.
translations.idiomatic: South-pointing carriage.

sentences.zh: 四周廂上施屋，指南人衣裙襦天衣，在廂中。

translations.literal: On all four sides of the compartment a roofed structure is set; a south-pointing man in skirt, robe, jacket, and celestial-pattern garment stands within the compartment.
translations.idiomatic: A roofed structure rose on every side of the compartment, with a south-pointing figure in skirt, robe, jacket, and celestial-pattern garment standing inside.

sentences.zh: 上四角皆施龍子竿，縣雜色真孔雀毦，烏布皁復幔，漆畫輪，駕牛，皆銅校飾。

translations.literal: On all four upper corners dragon-child poles are set; multicolored genuine peacock plumes are suspended; black cloth with black inner curtain; lacquer-painted wheels; ox-drawn; all with bronze fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-child poles stood at all four upper corners, suspending multicolored genuine peacock plumes; black cloth and a black inner curtain; lacquer-painted wheels; ox-drawn; all fittings were bronze.

sentences.zh: 記里鼓車。

translations.literal: Mile-drum carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Mile-drum carriage.

sentences.zh: 制如指南，上施華蓋子，衣漆畫，鼓機皆在內。

translations.literal: Its form like the south-pointing [carriage]; on top a flowered canopy is set; lacquer-painted; the drum mechanism is all within.
translations.idiomatic: Built like the south-pointing carriage, it bore a flowered canopy on top, lacquer-painted, with the drum mechanism housed entirely within.

sentences.zh: 輦車，如犢車，竹蓬。

translations.literal: Palanquin carriage, like a calf cart, with bamboo awning.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin carriage resembled a calf cart, with a bamboo awning.

sentences.zh: 廂外鑿鏤金薄，碧紗衣，織成芚，錦衣。

translations.literal: Outside the compartment, carved openwork gold leaf; green gauze garment; woven-pattern matting; brocade clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the compartment were carved openwork gold leaf, green gauze garments, woven matting, and brocade clothing.

sentences.zh: 廂裏及仰頂隱膝後戶，金塗鏤面，瑇瑁帖，金塗松精，登仙花紐，綠四緣，四望紗萌子，上下前後眉，鏤鍱。

translations.literal: Inside the compartment and on the upward-facing top, hidden knee and rear door; gilt openwork facing; tortoiseshell appliqué; gilt pine essence; ascending-immortal flower clasps; green four-border trim; four-view gauze awning; upper, lower, front, and rear brows; openwork plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the compartment and on the upward-facing roof were the hidden knee and rear door, gilt openwork facing, tortoiseshell appliqué, gilt pine essence, ascending-immortal flower clasps, green four-border trim, a four-view gauze awning, brows front and back above and below, and openwork plaques.

sentences.zh: 轅枕長角龍，白牙蘭，瑇瑁金塗校飾。

translations.literal: Shaft pillow [with] long-horned dragon; white ivory orchid; tortoiseshell and gilt fittings.
translations.idiomatic: The shaft pillow bore a long-horned dragon, white ivory orchid, and tortoiseshell with gilt fittings.

sentences.zh: 漆鄣塵板在蘭前，金銀花獸玃天龍師子鏤面，榆花鈿指子摩尼炎，金龍虎。

translations.literal: Lacquer dust-screen board before the orchid; gold and silver floral beasts, heaven-reaching dragon, lion openwork facing; elm-flower inlay, finger-guard, mani flame; gold dragon and tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Before the orchid stood a lacquer dust-screen board with openwork facing of gold and silver floral beasts, a heaven-reaching dragon, and lions; elm-flower inlay, finger-guards, mani flame, and gold dragon and tiger.

sentences.zh: 扶轅，銀口帶，龍板頭。

translations.literal: Shaft supports; silver mouth-band; dragon board head.
translations.idiomatic: Shaft supports, silver mouth-bands, and dragon board heads.

sentences.zh: 龍轅軛上，金鳳皇鈴璅，銀口帶，星後梢，瑇瑁帖，金塗香沓，銀星花獸幔竿杖，金塗龍牽，縱橫長，背花香染兆牀副。

translations.literal: On the dragon shaft yoke, gilt phoenix bells and links; silver mouth-band; star rear tip; tortoiseshell appliqué; gilt fragrant tread; silver star floral beast curtain-pole staff; gilt dragon draw; lengthwise and crosswise long [pieces]; back floral incense-dyed omen bed adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: On the dragon shaft yoke were gilt phoenix bells and links, silver mouth-bands, star rear tips, tortoiseshell appliqué, gilt fragrant tread, silver star floral beast curtain-pole staffs, gilt dragon draws, lengthwise and crosswise long pieces, and a back floral incense-dyed omen-bed adjunct.

sentences.zh: 自輦以下，二宮御車，皆綠油幢，絳系絡。

translations.literal: From the palanquin downward, the two palaces' imperial carriages all had green oil canopies and crimson cord netting.
translations.idiomatic: From the palanquin carriage downward, imperial carriages of the two palaces all bore green oil canopies and crimson cord netting.

sentences.zh: 御所乘，雙棟。

translations.literal: That which the sovereign rides has double ridgepoles.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's carriage had double ridgepoles.

sentences.zh: 其公主則碧油幢云。

translations.literal: For princesses it is the blue-green oil canopy, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses, it is said, used the blue-green oil canopy.

sentences.zh: 《司馬法》曰「夏后氏輦曰金車，殷曰胡奴車，周曰輜車」，皆輦也。

translations.literal: The Methods of Sima says, "Under the Xia the palanquin was called the Golden Carriage; under Yin the Barbarian-Servant Carriage; under Zhou the Supply Carriage"—all are palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: The Methods of Sima says: "Under the Xia the palanquin was called the Golden Carriage; under Yin the Barbarian-Servant Carriage; under Zhou the Supply Carriage"—all names for the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 《漢書叔孫通傳》云「皇帝輦出房」，成帝輦過後宮，此朝宴竝用也。

translations.literal: The Biography of Shusun Tong in the Book of Han says, "When the emperor's palanquin left the side chamber"; Emperor Cheng's palanquin passed through the rear palaces—both court and banquet used it alike.
translations.idiomatic: The Biography of Shusun Tong in the Book of Han says, "When the emperor's palanquin left the side chamber"; Emperor Cheng's palanquin passed through the rear palaces—court and banquet alike employed it.

sentences.zh: 《輿服志》云「輦車具金銀丹青采雘雕畫蒲陶之文，乘人以行」。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Carriages and Dress says, "The palanquin carriage has gold, silver, cinnabar, green, and polychrome carving and painted grapevine designs; men carry it and it moves."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Carriages and Dress says: "The palanquin carriage bore gold, silver, cinnabar, green, and polychrome carving with painted grapevine designs; bearers carried it forward."

sentences.zh: 信陽侯陰就見井丹，左右人進輦，是爲臣下亦得乘之。

translations.literal: Marquis Yin of Xinyang, when he went to see Jing Dan, had his attendants bring a palanquin—thus even subjects below the throne could ride it.
translations.idiomatic: When Marquis Yin of Xinyang went to see Jing Dan, his attendants brought a palanquin—showing that even subjects might ride it.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝給安平獻王孚雲母輦。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin granted the Prince of Anping, Xian, Fu, a mica palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin granted Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu, a mica palanquin.

sentences.zh: 晉中朝又有香衣輦，江左唯御所乘。

translations.literal: In the Jin central court there was also the incense-garment palanquin; east of the Yangtze only the sovereign rode it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin central court also had an incense-garment palanquin; east of the Yangtze only the sovereign rode it.

sentences.zh: 卧輦。

translations.literal: Reclining palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Reclining palanquin.

sentences.zh: 校飾如坐輦，不甚服用。

translations.literal: Fittings like the seated palanquin; not much used.
translations.idiomatic: Its fittings matched the seated palanquin; it was little used.

sentences.zh: 漆畫輪車，金塗校飾如輦，微有減降。

translations.literal: Lacquer-painted wheel carriage; gilt fittings like the palanquin, slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: A lacquer-painted wheel carriage with gilt fittings like the palanquin, but somewhat reduced.

sentences.zh: 金塗鐺，縱容後輠師子副也。

translations.literal: Gilt hub-bands; longitudinal adjuster, rear adjuster, lion adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: Gilt hub-bands, with longitudinal adjuster, rear adjuster, and lion adjunct.

sentences.zh: 御爲羣公舉哀臨哭所乘。

translations.literal: What the sovereign rides when leading mourning and weeping for the assembled lords.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign rode it when leading mourning and weeping for the assembled lords.

sentences.zh: 皇后太子妃亦乘之。

translations.literal: The empress and crown prince's consort also rode it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and the crown prince's consort rode it as well.

sentences.zh: 漆畫牽車，小形如輿車，金塗縱容後路師子輠，鐵鐺，錦衣。

translations.literal: Lacquer-painted draw carriage, small in form like the litter carriage; gilt longitudinal adjuster, rear road, lion adjuster; iron hub-bands; brocade clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The lacquer-painted draw carriage was small, shaped like the litter carriage, with gilt longitudinal adjuster, rear road, and lion adjuster, iron hub-bands, and brocade clothing.

sentences.zh: 廂裏隱膝後戶牙蘭，轅枕梢，幰竿戍棟樑，皆金塗校飾。

translations.literal: Inside the compartment, hidden knee and rear door, ivory orchid; shaft pillow tip; curtain pole, garrison ridgebeam—all gilt fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Inside were the hidden knee and rear door, ivory orchid, shaft-pillow tip, and curtain pole and garrison ridgebeam, all with gilt fittings.

sentences.zh: 御及皇太子所乘，卽古之羊車也。

translations.literal: What the sovereign and crown prince ride is the ancient goat carriage.
translations.idiomatic: What the sovereign and crown prince rode was the ancient goat carriage.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始中，中護軍羊琇乘羊車，爲司隷校尉劉毅所奏。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Jin, Central Protector of the Army Yang Xiu rode a goat carriage and was impeached by Director of the Imperial Secretariat Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taishi, Central Protector of the Army Yang Xiu rode a goat carriage and was impeached by Director of the Imperial Secretariat Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 武帝詔曰：「羊車雖無制，非素者所服，免官。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's edict said: "Although the goat carriage has no fixed rule, it is not what the plain-dressed should use—dismiss him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's edict said: "Although the goat carriage has no fixed regulation, it is not for those of plain station—dismiss him from office."

sentences.zh: 」《衞玠傳》云：「總角乘羊車，市人聚觀。

translations.literal: " The Biography of Wei Jie says: "In his boyhood he rode a goat carriage, and townspeople gathered to watch.
translations.idiomatic: The Biography of Wei Jie says: "In his boyhood he rode a goat carriage, and townspeople gathered to watch."

sentences.zh: 」今不駕羊，猶呼牽此車者爲羊車云。

translations.literal: " Today goats are no longer yoked, yet drawn carriages of this kind are still called goat carriages, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Today goats are no longer yoked, yet carriages drawn in this fashion are still called goat carriages.

sentences.zh: 輿車，形如軺車，柒畫，金校飾，錦衣。

translations.literal: Litter carriage, shaped like a light carriage; lacquer-painted; gilt fittings; brocade clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The litter carriage was shaped like a light carriage, lacquer-painted, with gilt fittings and brocade clothing.

sentences.zh: 兩廂後戶隱膝牙蘭，皆瑇瑁帖，刀格，鏤面花釘。

translations.literal: On both compartments, rear door, hidden knee, and ivory orchid—all tortoiseshell appliqué, blade lattices, openwork facing and floral nails.
translations.idiomatic: On both compartments, the rear door, hidden knee, and ivory orchid all bore tortoiseshell appliqué, blade lattices, and openwork facing with floral nails.

sentences.zh: 幰竿成校棟樑，下施八棡，金塗沓，兆牀副。

translations.literal: Curtain pole forming fitted ridgebeam; below, eight corner braces; gilt tread; omen-bed adjunct.
translations.idiomatic: The curtain pole formed a fitted ridgebeam; below were eight corner braces, gilt tread, and an omen-bed adjunct.

sentences.zh: 人舉之。

translations.literal: Men lift it.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers lifted it.

sentences.zh: 一曰小輿，小行幸乘之。

translations.literal: Also called small litter; used for minor progressions of the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Also called the small litter, it served for minor progressions of the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 皇太子亦得於宮內乘之。

translations.literal: The crown prince might also ride it within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince might also ride it within the palace.

sentences.zh: 衣書十二乘，澬榆轂輪，箕子壁，綠油衣，廂外綠紗萌，油幢絡，通幰，竿刺代棟樑，柮檽真形龍牽，支子花。

translations.literal: Twelve book-and-robe [carriages]; elm hubs and wheels; matting compartment walls; green oil clothing; outside the compartment green gauze awning; oil-canopy netting; full curtain; pole piercing substitute ridgebeam; hardwood true-form dragon draw; branch-flower.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve book-and-robe carriages with elm hubs and wheels, matting compartment walls, green oil clothing, green gauze awnings outside the compartment, oil-canopy netting, full curtains, poles piercing substitute ridgebeams, hardwood true-form dragon draws, and branch-flowers.

sentences.zh: 轅後伏神抗、承泥、沓，金塗校具。

translations.literal: Behind the shaft, crouching spirit strut, mud-bearer, and tread—all gilt fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the shaft were the crouching-spirit strut, mud-bearer, and tread, all gilt fittings.

sentences.zh: 古副車之象也。

translations.literal: The image of the ancient outrider carriage.
translations.idiomatic: This preserved the form of the ancient outrider carriage.

sentences.zh: 今亦曰五時副車。

translations.literal: Today it is also called the five-season outrider carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is also called the five-season outrider carriage.

sentences.zh: 青萌車，是謂潝幔車。

translations.literal: Green Awning carriage—called the steep-curtain carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Green Awning carriage—called the steep-curtain carriage.

sentences.zh: 油絡畫安車，公主、王妃、三公特進夫人所乘。

translations.literal: Secure carriage with oil netting and painted design—ridden by princesses, princess consorts, and grandees of the three ranks and specially advanced ladies.
translations.idiomatic: The secure carriage with oil netting and painted design was for princesses, princess consorts, and ladies of grandees of the three ranks and specially advanced rank.

sentences.zh: 漢制，皇后貴人紫罽軿車。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations, the empress and honored consorts used purple felt light carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han regulations, the empress and honored consorts rode purple felt light carriages.

sentences.zh: 晉皇后乘雲母油畫安車，駕六，以兩轅安車駕五爲副。

translations.literal: Under Jin the empress rode a mica oil-painted secure carriage, drawn by six; a two-shaft secure carriage drawn by five served as outrider.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin the empress rode a mica oil-painted secure carriage with six horses; a two-shaft secure carriage drawn by five served as outrider.

sentences.zh: 公主畫安車駕六，以兩轅安車駕三爲副。

translations.literal: Princesses rode painted comfort carriages drawn by six; two-shaft comfort carriages drawn by three served as escort.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses used painted comfort carriages with teams of six, escorted by two-shaft comfort carriages with teams of three.

sentences.zh: 公主畫安車駕三，三夫人青交絡安車駕三，皆以紫絳罽軿車駕三爲副。

translations.literal: Princesses rode painted comfort carriages drawn by three; the three Ladies rode green interlaced comfort carriages drawn by three—all used purple-crimson felt enclosed carriages drawn by three as escort.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses rode painted comfort carriages with three horses; the three Ladies rode green interlaced comfort carriages with three horses—each rank was escorted by a purple-crimson felt enclosed carriage with three horses.

sentences.zh: 九嬪世婦軿車駕二，王公妃特進夫人皁交絡爲副。

translations.literal: The nine concubines and palace ladies rode enclosed carriages drawn by two; princes' consorts and specially advanced ladies used black interlaced carriages as escort.
translations.idiomatic: The nine concubines and palace ladies rode enclosed carriages with two horses; princes' consorts and specially advanced ladies were escorted by black interlaced carriages.

sentences.zh: 漢賤軺車而貴軿車，晉賤輜軿而貴軺車，皆行禮所乘。

translations.literal: Han ranked the light chariot low and the enclosed carriage high; Jin ranked supply and enclosed carriages low and the light chariot high—all were used in ceremonial travel.
translations.idiomatic: Han ceremony favored enclosed carriages over light chariots; Jin reversed that, favoring light chariots over supply and enclosed types—all were ritual travel vehicles.

sentences.zh: 黃屋車，建碧旂九旒，九旒，鸞輅也。

translations.literal: Yellow Canopy carriage: it bore a green banner with nine tassels; nine tassels is the phoenix regalia carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Canopy carriage bore a green banner with nine tassels—the nine-tassel standard of the phoenix regalia carriage.

sentences.zh: 《漢輿服志》云：「金根車，蓋黃繒爲裏，謂之黃屋。

translations.literal: The Book of Han, Carriages and Dress, says: 「The Golden Root carriage has a canopy lined with yellow silk—this is called the Yellow Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han, Carriages and Dress, records: 「The Golden Root carriage has a canopy lined with yellow silk, and is called the Yellow Canopy.

sentences.zh: 」今金、玉輅皆以黃地錦，唯此車以黃繒。

translations.literal: 」Today the gold and jade regalia chariots all use yellow-ground brocade; only this carriage uses yellow silk.
translations.idiomatic: 」Today the gold and jade regalia chariots all use yellow-ground brocade; only this carriage still uses yellow silk.

sentences.zh: 皆金塗校具，黃隱隨陰，青毛羽，二十八爪支子花，絳系絡。

translations.literal: All have gold-plated fittings, yellow shade ornaments, green feather plumes, twenty-eight-claw branch-flower motifs, and crimson cord networks.
translations.idiomatic: All fittings were gold-plated, with yellow shade ornaments, green feather plumes, twenty-eight-claw branch-flower motifs, and crimson cord networks.

sentences.zh: 九命上公所乘。

translations.literal: Ridden by upper dukes of the nine commands.
translations.idiomatic: It was ridden by upper dukes of the nine commands.

sentences.zh: 青蓋安車，朱轓漆班輪，駕一，左右騑，通幰車爲副，諸王禮行所乘。

translations.literal: Green-canopy comfort carriage, vermilion skirt boards and lacquered spotted wheels, one team, flanking outriders, full-canopy carriage as escort—ridden by princes on ritual journeys.
translations.idiomatic: The green-canopy comfort carriage had vermilion skirt boards and lacquered spotted wheels, a single team with flanking outriders, and a full-canopy escort carriage—used by princes on ritual journeys.

sentences.zh: 凡車有轓者謂之軒。

translations.literal: Any carriage with skirt boards is called a high carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Any carriage with skirt boards was called a high carriage.

sentences.zh: 皁蓋安車，朱轓漆班輪，駕一，通幰牛車爲副，三公禮行所乘。

translations.literal: Black-canopy comfort carriage, vermilion skirt boards and lacquered spotted wheels, one team, full-canopy ox cart as escort—ridden by the three excellencies on ritual journeys.
translations.idiomatic: The black-canopy comfort carriage had vermilion skirt boards and lacquered spotted wheels, a single team, and a full-canopy ox cart as escort—used by the three excellencies on ritual journeys.

sentences.zh: 安車，黑耳皁蓋馬車，朱轓，駕一，牛車爲副，國公列侯禮行所乘。

translations.literal: Comfort carriage: black-eared black-canopy horse carriage with vermilion skirt boards, one team, ox cart as escort—ridden by state dukes and marquises on ritual journeys.
translations.idiomatic: The comfort carriage was a black-eared, black-canopy horse carriage with vermilion skirt boards, one team, and an ox cart as escort—used by state dukes and marquises on ritual journeys.

sentences.zh: 馬車，駕一，九卿、領、護、二衞、驍游、四軍、五校從郊陵所乘。

translations.literal: Horse carriage, one team—ridden by the nine ministers, bureau chiefs, the two guards, swift and roaming units, the four armies, and the five regiments when attending suburban rites and imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The horse carriage, with one team, was used by the nine ministers, bureau chiefs, the two guards, swift and roaming units, the four armies, and the five regiments when attending suburban rites and imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 晉制，三公下至九卿，又各安車黑耳一乘，公駕三，特進駕二，卿駕一，復各軺車施黑耳後戶皁輪一乘。

translations.literal: Under Jin regulations, from the three excellencies down to the nine ministers each also had one black-eared comfort carriage: dukes with three horses, specially advanced with two, ministers with one; each also had a light chariot with black ears, a rear door, and black wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin rules, from the three excellencies down to the nine ministers each kept a black-eared comfort carriage—three horses for dukes, two for specially advanced officers, one for ministers—and each also had a light chariot with black ears, a rear door, and black wheels.

sentences.zh: 油絡軺車，尚書令、僕射、中書監、令、尚書、侍中、常侍、中黃門、中書、散騎侍郎，皆駕一牛，朝直所乘。

translations.literal: Oil-network light chariot: the Director of the Masters of Writing, vice directors, directors of the Secretariat, masters of writing, palace attendants, regular attendants, palace eunuchs, secretariat aides, and attendant cavalry aides all drove one ox—used on morning duty at court.
translations.idiomatic: The oil-network light chariot was drawn by a single ox for the director and vice directors of the masters of writing, secretariat directors and masters, palace and regular attendants, palace eunuchs, secretariat aides, and attendant cavalry aides on morning court duty.

sentences.zh: 晉制，尚書令施黑耳後戶皁輪，僕射、中書監、令直施後戶皁輪，尚書無後戶，皆漆輪轂，今猶然。

translations.literal: Under Jin regulations, the Director of the Masters of Writing had black ears, a rear door, and black wheels; vice directors and secretariat directors had a rear door and black wheels; masters of writing had no rear door—all had lacquered wheel hubs, and the rule still held.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin rules the director of the masters of writing had black ears, a rear door, and black wheels; vice directors and secretariat directors had a rear door and black wheels; masters of writing had no rear door—all with lacquered hubs, as still observed.

sentences.zh: 安車，赤屏，駕一，又軺車，施後戶，爲副，太子二傅禮行所乘。

translations.literal: Comfort carriage with red screen, one team; also a light chariot with a rear door as escort—ridden by the crown prince's two tutors on ritual journeys.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's two tutors used a comfort carriage with a red screen and one team, escorted by a light chariot with a rear door, on ritual journeys.

sentences.zh: 四望車，通幰，油幢絡，班柒輪轂。

translations.literal: Four-view carriage: full canopy, oil-treated banner network, lacquered spotted wheel hubs.
translations.idiomatic: The four-view carriage had a full canopy, an oil-treated banner network, and lacquered spotted wheel hubs.

sentences.zh: 亦曰皁輪，以加禮貴臣。

translations.literal: Also called the black-wheeled carriage, for ministers granted added ritual honors.
translations.idiomatic: It was also called the black-wheeled carriage, reserved for ministers granted added ritual honors.

sentences.zh: 晉武詔給魏舒陽燧四望小車。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin by edict granted Wei Shu a yangsui mirror and a small four-view carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin by edict granted Wei Shu a yangsui mirror and a small four-view carriage.

sentences.zh: 三望車，制度如四望。

translations.literal: Three-view carriage: regulations like the four-view.
translations.idiomatic: The three-view carriage followed the same regulations as the four-view.

sentences.zh: 或謂之夾望，亦以加禮貴臣。

translations.literal: Some call it the paired-view carriage; it too was for ministers granted added ritual honors.
translations.idiomatic: Some called it the paired-view carriage; it too was for ministers granted added ritual honors.

sentences.zh: 次四望。

translations.literal: It ranked below the four-view.
translations.idiomatic: It ranked below the four-view.

sentences.zh: 油幢絡車，制似三望而減。

translations.literal: Oil-banner network carriage: made like the three-view but reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The oil-banner network carriage was built like the three-view but with reduced ornament.

sentences.zh: 王公加禮者之常乘，次三望。

translations.literal: The regular carriage of princes and dukes granted added honors, ranking below the three-view.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and dukes granted added honors used it as their regular carriage; it ranked below the three-view.

sentences.zh: 平乘車，竹箕子壁仰，榆爲輪，通幰竿刺代棟樑，柮檽真形龍牽，金塗支子花紐，轅頭後梢沓伏神承泥。

translations.literal: Level-riding carriage: bamboo mat walls and upward-facing boards, elm wheels, full-canopy pole piercing the substitute ridge beam, true-form dragon traces in catalpa and chestnut, gold-plated branch-flower clasps, dragon traces at the yoke head and rear tip, stacked spirit figures and mud-bearers at the shaft foot.
translations.idiomatic: The level-riding carriage had bamboo mat walls and upward-facing boards, elm wheels, a full-canopy pole piercing the substitute ridge beam, true-form dragon traces in catalpa and chestnut, gold-plated branch-flower clasps, and dragon traces at the yoke head and rear tip with stacked spirit figures and mud-bearers at the shaft foot.

sentences.zh: 庶人亦然，但不通幰。

translations.literal: Commoners used it likewise, but without the full canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners used the same type, but without the full canopy.

sentences.zh: 三公諸王所乘。

translations.literal: Ridden by the three excellencies and princes.
translations.idiomatic: It was ridden by the three excellencies and princes.

sentences.zh: 自四望至平乘，皆銅校飾。

translations.literal: From the four-view down to the level-riding, all had copper-plated fittings.
translations.idiomatic: From the four-view down to the level-riding, all fittings were copper-plated.

sentences.zh: 轀輬車。

translations.literal: Hearse carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Hearse carriage.

sentences.zh: 四輪，飾如金根。

translations.literal: Four wheels; ornament like the Golden Root.
translations.idiomatic: It had four wheels and ornament like the Golden Root carriage.

sentences.zh: 四角龍首，施組銜璧，垂五采，析羽葆流蘇，前後雲氣錯畫帷裳，以素爲池而黼黻。

translations.literal: Dragon heads at the four corners, cords bearing jade disks, hanging five colors, split feather canopies and tassels, cloud patterns painted on curtains front and back, plain ground with fu and fu motifs.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon heads stood at the four corners, with cords bearing jade disks, five-colored hangings, split feather canopies and tassels, and cloud patterns painted on the curtains front and back over a plain ground with fu and fu motifs.

sentences.zh: 駕四白駱馬，太僕執轡。

translations.literal: Drawn by four white camels; the Grand Master of Horse held the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Four white camels drew it while the Grand Master of Horse held the reins.

sentences.zh: 貴臣薨，亦如之，羽飾駕御，微有減降。

translations.literal: When an honored minister died, the same was used; feather ornament and teams were slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When an honored minister died, the same carriage was used, with feather ornament and teams slightly reduced.

sentences.zh: 《虞書》曰：「予欲觀古人之象，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲作繢，宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻絺繡，以五采章施于五色。

translations.literal: The Book of Yu says: 「I wish to view the images of antiquity—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, and patterned creatures embroidered; ancestral vessels, algae, fire, rice powder, fu and fu in fine silk, with the five colors displayed on the five hues.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yu says: 「I wish to view the images of antiquity—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, and patterned creatures embroidered; ancestral vessels, algae, fire, rice powder, fu and fu in fine silk, with the five colors displayed on the five hues.

sentences.zh: 」天子服備日、月以下，公山、龍以下，侯伯華蟲以下，子男藻、火以下，卿大夫粉米以下。

translations.literal: 」The Son of Heaven's dress included the sun and moon and below; the duke mountains and dragons and below; marquis and earl patterned creatures and below; viscount and baron algae and fire and below; ministers and grand masters rice powder and below.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Son of Heaven's robes bore the sun and moon and all below them; a duke bore mountains and dragons and below; a marquis or earl bore patterned creatures and below; a viscount or baron bore algae and fire and below; ministers and grand masters bore rice powder and below.

sentences.zh: 天子六冕，王后六服，著在周官。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had six crowns and the empress six garments, set forth in the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven had six crowns and the empress six garments, as set forth in the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 公侯以下，咸有名則，佩玉組綬，竝具禮文，後代沿革，見《漢志晉服制令》，其冠十三品，見蔡邕《獨斷》，竝不復具詳。

translations.literal: Below duke and marquis all had named regulations, jade pendants and cord sashes, all fully specified in ritual texts; later changes appear in the Han Treatise and Jin dress regulations—the thirteen crown grades appear in Cai Yong's Duduan; they are not detailed here.
translations.idiomatic: Below duke and marquis every rank had named rules for jade pendants and cord sashes, all spelled out in ritual texts; later changes appear in the Han Treatise and Jin dress regulations, and the thirteen crown grades in Cai Yong's Duduan—not repeated here.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始四年，更制五輅，議脩五冕，朝會饗獵，各有所服，事見《宋注》。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, Emperor Ming of Song revised the five regalia chariots and deliberated restoring the five crowns; court assembly, feasts, and hunts each had its own dress—the matter appears in the Song commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi, Emperor Ming of Song revised the five regalia chariots and debated restoring the five crowns; court assembly, feasts, and hunts each had its own dress, as recorded in the Song commentaries.

sentences.zh: 舊相承三公以下冕七旒，青玉珠，卿大夫以下五旒，黑玉珠。

translations.literal: By long-standing practice, below the three excellencies the crown had seven tassels with blue jade beads; below ministers and grand masters, five tassels with black jade beads.
translations.idiomatic: By long practice, ranks below the three excellencies wore crowns of seven tassels with blue jade beads; ministers and grand masters wore five tassels with black jade beads.

sentences.zh: 永明六年，太常丞何諲之議，案《周禮》命數，改三公八旒，卿六旒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming, Director of Rites Assistant He Yin-zhi proposed, following the Zhou Rites rank numbers, to change the three excellencies to eight tassels and ministers to six.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongming, Director of Rites Assistant He Yin-zhi proposed, on the Zhou Rites rank scheme, to raise the three excellencies to eight tassels and ministers to six.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉議，依漢三公服，山、龍九章，卿華蟲七章。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian proposed following Han dress for the three excellencies—mountains and dragons in nine sections—and for ministers, patterned creatures in seven sections.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian proposed following Han practice: nine sections of mountains and dragons for the three excellencies, seven sections of patterned creatures for ministers.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted it.

sentences.zh: 平冕黑介幘，今謂平天冠。

translations.literal: Flat crown with black jie cap—today called the flat heaven crown.
translations.idiomatic: The flat crown with black jie cap is today called the flat heaven crown.

sentences.zh: 皁表朱緣裏，廣七尺，長尺二寸，垂珠十二旒，以朱組爲纓，如其綬色。

translations.literal: Black exterior with vermilion border and lining, seven chi wide and one chi two cun long, hanging twelve tassel pearls; vermilion cords as the chin strap, matching the sash color.
translations.idiomatic: It had a black exterior with vermilion border and lining, seven chi wide and one chi two cun long, with twelve hanging pearl tassels; vermilion cords served as the chin strap, matching the sash color.

sentences.zh: 衣皁上絳下，裳前三幅，後四幅。

translations.literal: Robe black above and crimson below; skirt three panels in front and four behind.
translations.idiomatic: The robe was black above and crimson below; the skirt had three panels in front and four behind.

sentences.zh: 衣畫而裳繡，爲日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻十二章。

translations.literal: The robe was painted and the skirt embroidered with the twelve insignia: sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, patterned creatures, algae, fire, rice powder, fu, and fu.
translations.idiomatic: The robe was painted and the skirt embroidered with the twelve insignia—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, patterned creatures, algae, fire, rice powder, fu, and fu.

sentences.zh: 素帶廣四寸，朱裏，以朱綠裨飾其側，要中以朱，垂以綠，垂三尺。

translations.literal: Plain belt four cun wide with vermilion lining; vermilion and green trim on the sides; vermilion at the center, green pendants three chi long.
translations.idiomatic: The plain belt was four cun wide with vermilion lining, vermilion-green trim at the sides, vermilion at the center, and green pendants three chi long.

sentences.zh: 中衣，以絳緣其領袖，赤皮韍，絳袴袜，赤舄，郊廟臨朝所服也。

translations.literal: Inner robe with crimson at collar and sleeves, red leather knee covers, crimson trousers and socks, and red shoes—worn at suburban temples and court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe had crimson at collar and sleeves, with red leather knee covers, crimson trousers and socks, and red shoes—worn at suburban temples and when holding court audience.

sentences.zh: 漢世冕用白玉珠爲旒。

translations.literal: In the Han, coronets used white jade beads for the tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, coronets hung white jade beads as tassels.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝好婦人飾，改以珊瑚珠。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei favored women's ornaments and changed them to coral beads.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei, taken with women's finery, replaced them with coral beads.

sentences.zh: 晉初仍舊，後乃改。

translations.literal: Early Jin still followed the old practice; only later was it changed again.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin kept the old way; only later did the court change it again.

sentences.zh: 江左以美玉難得，遂用琫珠，世謂之白琁珠。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze, fine jade was hard to obtain, so peng beads were used instead—called white xuan beads.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze fine jade grew scarce, and peng beads stood in—known as white xuan beads.

sentences.zh: 袞衣，漢世出陳留襄邑所織。

translations.literal: The sacrificial robe in Han times came from weaving at Xiangyi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial robe under the Han was woven at Xiangyi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 宋末用繡及織成，建武中，明帝以織成重，乃采畫爲之，加飾金銀薄，世亦謂爲天衣。

translations.literal: Late Song used embroidery and woven brocade; in the Jianwu era Ming Di found woven brocade too heavy and switched to painted designs trimmed with gold and silver foil—also called "heavenly garments."
translations.idiomatic: Late Song favored embroidery and woven brocade; in the Jianwu years Ming Di judged brocade too heavy and had the robe painted instead, edged with gold and silver foil—also called heavenly garments.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：黼黻之設，經緯爲用，故五色六章十二衣還相爲質也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Fu and fu ornament depends on warp and weft; hence five colors, six patterns, and twelve garments alternate as their ground.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Fu and fu depend on warp and weft—five colors, six patterns, twelve garments taking turns as the ground.

sentences.zh: 歷代龍袞，織以成文，今體不勝衣，變易舊法，豈致美黻冕之謂乎！

translations.literal: Through the ages dragon robes were woven into their patterns; today's cut cannot bear the robe's weight, and old methods are altered—can this be what is meant by perfecting the beauty of fu crowns?
translations.idiomatic: Age after age, dragon robes were woven into their patterns; now the cut cannot carry the cloth, and the old law is bent—can this be the beauty fu crowns were meant to hold?

sentences.zh: 通天冠，黑介幘，金博山顏，絳紗袍，皁緣中衣，乘輿常朝所服。

translations.literal: Penetrating-Heaven crown, black jie cap, golden Mount Bo brow, crimson gauze robe, black-bordered inner robe—the emperor's regular court dress when riding the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Penetrating-Heaven crown, black jie cap, golden Mount Bo brow, crimson gauze robe, black-bordered inner robe—what the emperor wore at ordinary court when riding the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 舊用駮犀簪導，東昏改用玉。

translations.literal: Formerly mottled rhinoceros horn hairpins guided the cap; Donghun changed them to jade.
translations.idiomatic: Once mottled rhinoceros horn hairpins guided the cap; Donghun switched them to jade.

sentences.zh: 其朝服，臣下皆同。

translations.literal: For court dress, ministers and subordinates all matched.
translations.idiomatic: For court dress, ministers and subordinates dressed the same.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘，單衣，無定色，乘輿拜陵所服。

translations.literal: Black jie cap and single-layer garment of no fixed color—worn when the emperor rode out to pay tomb rites.
translations.idiomatic: Black jie cap and a single-layer robe of no fixed hue—worn when the emperor rode out to bow at the tombs.

sentences.zh: 其白帢單衣，謂之素服，以舉哀臨喪。

translations.literal: The white headcloth and single-layer garment were called plain dress, worn to lead mourning at funerals.
translations.idiomatic: A white headcloth with a single-layer robe was called plain dress, for leading mourning at a funeral.

sentences.zh: 遠游冠，太子諸王所冠。

translations.literal: Far-Travel crown—worn by crown prince and princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Far-Travel crown was worn by the crown prince and by princes.

sentences.zh: 太子朱纓，翠羽緌珠節。

translations.literal: The crown prince had a vermilion tassel with kingfisher-feather cord and pearl knots.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wore a vermilion tassel, kingfisher-feather cord, and knotted pearls.

sentences.zh: 諸王玄纓，公侯皆同。

translations.literal: Princes had a dark tassel; dukes and marquises the same.
translations.idiomatic: Princes wore a dark tassel; dukes and marquises did likewise.

sentences.zh: 平冕，各以組爲纓，王公八旒，衣山、龍九章，卿七旒，衣華蟲七章，竝助祭所服。

translations.literal: Flat crown: each rank used cord as tassel—princes and dukes eight tassels, robes with mountains and dragons in nine sections; ministers seven tassels, robes with patterned creatures in seven sections—all worn when assisting at sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The flat crown: each rank had cord for a tassel—princes and dukes eight tassels, robes of mountains and dragons in nine sections; ministers seven tassels, robes of patterned creatures in seven sections—all for assisting at sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 皆畫皂絳繒爲之。

translations.literal: All were made by painting black and crimson silk.
translations.idiomatic: All were made from black and crimson silk, painted.

sentences.zh: 進賢冠，諸開國公、侯，鄉、亭侯，卿，大夫，尚書，關內侯，二千石，博士，中書郎，丞、郎，祕書監、丞、郎，太子中舍人、洗馬、舍人，諸府長史，卿，尹、丞，下至六百石令長小吏，以三梁、二梁、一梁爲差，事見《晉令》。

translations.literal: Advance-the-Worthy crown: from founding dukes and marquises through village and precinct marquises, ministers, grand masters, masters of writing, interior marquises, 2000-shi officials, erudites, secretariat aides, directors and aides of the secretariat, crown prince attendants, tutors, and stewards, prefectural chiefs and aides, down to magistrates and petty clerks at 600 shi—the difference was three beams, two beams, or one beam, as set out in the Jin regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Advance-the-Worthy crown: founding dukes and marquises, village and precinct marquises, ministers, grand masters, masters of writing, interior marquises, 2000-shi officers, erudites, secretariat aides, secretariat directors and aides, crown-prince attendants, tutors, and stewards, prefectural chiefs and aides, down to 600-shi magistrates and petty clerks—all distinguished by three beams, two beams, or one beam, as the Jin regulations record.

sentences.zh: 武冠，侍臣加貂蟬，餘軍校武職、黃門、散騎、太子中庶子、二率、朝散、都尉，皆冠之。

translations.literal: Military crown: attendant ministers added marten and cicada; other military officers, gate eunuchs, attendant cavalry, crown prince aides, guards, roaming attendants, and commandants all wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The military crown: court attendants added marten and cicada; military officers, gate eunuchs, attendant cavalry, crown-prince aides, the two guards, roaming attendants, and commandants all wore it.

sentences.zh: 唯武騎虎賁服文衣，插雉尾於武冠上。

translations.literal: Only martial riders and tiger guards wore patterned robes and thrust pheasant tails into the military crown.
translations.idiomatic: Only the martial riders and tiger guards wore patterned robes and set pheasant tails in the military crown.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：應劭《漢官》釋附蟬，及司馬彪志竝不見侍中與常侍有異，唯言左右珥貂而已。

translations.literal: The historian says: Ying Shao's Explanation of Han Offices glosses the attached cicada, and Sima Biao's treatise likewise sees no distinction between palace attendant and regular attendant—only that left and right wore marten at the ears.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Ying Shao's Explanation of Han Offices glosses the attached cicada, and Sima Biao's treatise likewise finds no difference between palace attendant and regular attendant—only that left and right wore marten at the ears.

sentences.zh: 案項氏說云「漢侍中蟬，刻爲蟬像，常侍但爲璫而不蟬」，未詳何代所改也。

translations.literal: Xiang's account runs: "Han palace attendants bore a cicada carved as a cicada; regular attendants had only the ring without the cicada"—which era made the change is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's note says: "Han palace attendants wore a cicada carved as a cicada; regular attendants had only the ring, no cicada"—which age altered that is not known.

sentences.zh: 法冠，廷尉等諸執法者冠之。

translations.literal: Law crown—worn by the director of justice and other law officers.
translations.idiomatic: The law crown was worn by the director of justice and other law officers.

sentences.zh: 高山冠，謁者冠之。

translations.literal: High Mountain crown—worn by ushers.
translations.idiomatic: The High Mountain crown was worn by ushers.

sentences.zh: 樊噲冠，殿門衞士冠之。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai crown—worn by palace gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Fan Kuai crown was worn by palace gate guards.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘冠，文冠；

translations.literal: Black jie-cap crown for civil officials;
translations.idiomatic: The black jie-cap crown was for civil officials;

sentences.zh: 平幘冠，武冠。

translations.literal: flat-cap crown for military officers.
translations.idiomatic: the flat-cap crown for military officers.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、僕射、尚書納言幘，後飾爲異。

translations.literal: Directors and vice directors of the masters of writing, and masters of writing receiving edicts— their caps later differed in ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Directors and vice directors of the masters of writing, and masters of writing who received edicts—their caps later differed in ornament.

sentences.zh: 童子空頂幘，施假髻，貴賤同服。

translations.literal: Boys wore hollow-top caps with false topknots; noble and humble dressed alike.
translations.idiomatic: Boys wore hollow-top caps with false topknots; high and low dressed the same.

sentences.zh: 救日蝕，文武官皆免冠，著赤介幘對朝服。

translations.literal: When responding to a solar eclipse, civil and military officials all removed their crowns and wore red jie caps over court dress.
translations.idiomatic: When rites answered a solar eclipse, civil and military officials all laid aside their crowns and wore red jie caps over court dress.

sentences.zh: 赤幘，示威武也。

translations.literal: The red cap displayed martial resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The red cap showed martial resolve.

sentences.zh: 袴褶，車駕親戎、中外纂嚴所服。

translations.literal: Trousers and jacket—worn when the imperial carriage took the field in person, or when court and camp assembled in full martial array.
translations.idiomatic: Trousers and jacket—worn when the emperor took the field in person, or when court and camp mustered in full martial array.

sentences.zh: 黑冠，帽綴紫褾，以絡帶代鞶帶。

translations.literal: Black crown with purple cap-band, using a cord belt in place of the leather girdle.
translations.idiomatic: Black crown with a purple cap-band, a cord belt standing in for the leather girdle.

sentences.zh: 中官紫褾，外官絳褾。

translations.literal: Inner officials used purple bands; outer officials used crimson bands.
translations.idiomatic: Inner officials wore purple bands; outer officials wore crimson bands.

sentences.zh: 其纂嚴戎服不綴褾，行留悉同。

translations.literal: For strict assembly, military dress had no border trim attached; whether traveling or staying, all were alike.
translations.idiomatic: Under strict assembly alert, military dress had no border trim; on the march or at rest, the rule was the same.

sentences.zh: 校獵巡幸，從官戎服革帶鞶帶，文官不纓，武官脫冠。

translations.literal: On hunt-inspection progress tours, attendants wore military dress with leather belt and girdle plaque; civil officials wore no cap cords; military officials removed their caps.
translations.idiomatic: On hunt-inspection tours and imperial progresses, attendants wore military dress with leather belt and plaque girdle; civil officials went without cap cords; military officials removed their caps.

sentences.zh: 袿大衣，謂之褘衣，皇后謁廟所服。

translations.literal: The gui great robe, called the hui robe, was what the empress wore when attending the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The gui great robe—called the hui robe—was the empress's dress for attending the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 公主會見大首髻，其燕服則施嚴雜寶爲佩瑞。

translations.literal: Princesses at audiences wore the great topknot headdress; for informal dress they displayed formal mixed jewels as pendant auspices.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses at audiences wore the great topknot crown; in informal dress they wore splendid mixed jewels as pendant regalia.

sentences.zh: 袿用繡爲衣，裳加五色，鏁金銀校飾。

translations.literal: Gui robes used embroidery for the upper garment; the skirt added five colors, with locked gold-and-silver trim ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Gui robes had embroidered upper garments and five-colored skirts, with locked gold-and-silver trim.

sentences.zh: 綬，乘輿黃赤綬，黃赤縹綠紺五采。

translations.literal: Cord sashes: the imperial vehicle used yellow-crimson sash—yellow, crimson, light blue, green, and dark blue, five colors.
translations.idiomatic: Cord sashes: the imperial equipage used yellow-crimson—five colors of yellow, crimson, light blue, green, and dark blue.

sentences.zh: 太子朱綬，諸王纁朱綬，皆赤黃縹紺四采。

translations.literal: The crown prince used vermilion sash; princes used tawny-crimson sash—all four colors of crimson, yellow, light blue, and dark blue.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wore a vermilion sash; princes wore tawny-crimson—each in four colors of crimson, yellow, light blue, and dark blue.

sentences.zh: 妃亦同。

translations.literal: Consorts were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial consorts followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 相國綠綟綬，三采，綠紫紺。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of State used a green patterned sash, three colors—green, purple, and dark blue.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor of state wore a green patterned sash in three colors—green, purple, and dark blue.

sentences.zh: 郡公玄朱，侯伯青朱，子男素朱，皆三采。

translations.literal: Commandery dukes black-crimson; marquises and earls blue-crimson; viscounts and barons plain crimson—all three colors.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery dukes black-crimson; marquises and earls blue-crimson; viscounts and barons plain crimson—all three-colored sashes.

sentences.zh: 公世子紫，侯世子青，鄉、亭、關內侯墨綬，皆二采。

translations.literal: Duke heirs purple; marquis heirs blue; township, precinct, and within-the-passes marquises black sash—all two colors.
translations.idiomatic: Ducal heirs purple; marquis heirs blue; township, precinct, and within-the-passes marquises black—all two-colored sashes.

sentences.zh: 郡國太守、內史青，尚書令、僕、中書監、令、祕書監皆黑，丞皆黃，諸府丞亦黃。

translations.literal: Commandery and principality administrators and inner administrators blue; directors and vice directors of the masters of writing, secretariat directors and commissioners, and archive director all black; assistants all yellow; all bureau assistants also yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery and principality administrators and inner administrators wore blue; directors and vice directors of the masters of writing, secretariat directors and commissioners, and the archive director wore black; all assistants wore yellow, as did bureau assistants throughout.
