sentences.zh: 皇后與乘輿同赤，貴嬪、夫人、貴人紫，王太妃、長公主、封君亦紫綬，六宮青綬，青白紅，郡公、侯夫人青綬。

translations.literal: The empress matched the imperial vehicle in crimson; honored consorts, ladies, and honored ladies purple; princes' grand consorts, chief princesses, and enfeoffed ladies also purple sash; the six palaces green sash—green, white, and red; commandery dukes' and marquises' consorts green sash.
translations.idiomatic: The empress matched the sovereign in crimson; honored consorts, ladies, and honored ladies wore purple; princes' grand consorts, chief princesses, and enfeoffed ladies also purple sashes; the six palaces green—green, white, and red; commandery dukes' and marquises' consorts green sashes.

sentences.zh: 乘輿傳國璽，秦璽也。

translations.literal: The imperial vehicle's Heirloom Seal of the realm was the Qin seal.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's Heirloom Seal of the realm was the Qin dynasty seal.

sentences.zh: 晉中原亂沒胡，江左初無之，北方人呼晉家爲「白板天子」。

translations.literal: When Jin's central plains fell into chaos it was lost to the barbarians; in the south at first they had none; northerners called the Jin house the "blank-board Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin central plains fell into chaos the seal was lost to the barbarians; the south at first had none, and northerners called the Jin court the "blank-board Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 冉閔敗，璽還南。

translations.literal: When Ran Min was defeated, the seal returned south.
translations.idiomatic: After Ran Min's defeat, the seal returned to the south.

sentences.zh: 別有行信等六璽，皆金爲之，亦秦、漢之制也。

translations.literal: Separately there were six seals including Traveling Credence, all made of gold—also the Qin and Han institution.
translations.idiomatic: There were also six seals, including the Traveling Credence, all of gold—the same Qin and Han system.

sentences.zh: 皇后金璽，太子諸王金璽，皆龜鈕。

translations.literal: The empress's gold seal and the crown prince's and princes' gold seals all had tortoise knobs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's gold seal and the gold seals of the crown prince and princes all bore tortoise knobs.

sentences.zh: 公侯五等金章，公世子金印，侯銀印，貴嬪、夫人金章，公主、王太妃、封君金印，六宮以下公侯太夫人夫人銀印。

translations.literal: Dukes and marquises of the five grades used gold seals; ducal heirs gold seals; marquis heirs silver seals; honored consorts and ladies gold seals; princesses, princes' grand consorts, and enfeoffed ladies gold seals; below the six palaces, grand consorts of dukes and marquises and ladies used silver seals.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises of the five grades wore gold seals; ducal heirs gold seals; marquis heirs silver; honored consorts and ladies gold; princesses, princes' grand consorts, and enfeoffed ladies gold; below the six palaces, grand consorts of dukes and marquises and their ladies silver.

sentences.zh: 其公、將軍金章，光祿大夫、卿、尹、太子傅、諸領護將軍、中郎將、校尉、郡國太守內史、四品五品將軍，皆銀章，尚書令、僕、中書監、令、祕書監丞、太子二率、諸府長史、卿、尹、丞、尉、中丞、都水使者、諸州刺史，皆銅印。

translations.literal: Dukes and generals used gold seals; Household Minister, ministers, chief administrators, crown prince tutors, all command and protect generals, palace gentlemen-commandants, commandants, commandery and principality administrators and inner administrators, and fourth- and fifth-rank generals all used silver seals; directors and vice directors of the masters of writing, secretariat directors and commissioners, archive director and aides, the crown prince's two commandants, all bureau chief clerks, ministers, chief administrators, assistants, commandants, imperial censors, directors of waterways, and provincial governors all used bronze seals.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and generals had gold seals; the household minister, ministers, chief administrators, crown prince tutors, command and protect generals, palace gentlemen-commandants, commandants, commandery and principality administrators and inner administrators, and fourth- and fifth-rank generals had silver; directors and vice directors of the masters of writing, secretariat directors and commissioners, archive director and aides, the crown prince's two commandants, bureau chief clerks, ministers, chief administrators, assistants, commandants, imperial censors, directors of waterways, and provincial governors had bronze.

sentences.zh: 三臺五省二品文官，皆簪白筆。

translations.literal: Second-rank civil officials of the Three Departments and Five Ministries all wore white writing brushes in the hair.
translations.idiomatic: Second-rank civil officials of the Three Departments and Five Ministries all wore white writing brushes in their hair.

sentences.zh: 王公五等及武官不簪，加內侍乃簪。

translations.literal: Princes of the five grades and martial officials did not wear them; only with added palace attendant status did they wear them.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the five grades and martial officials did not wear them; only when also serving as palace attendants did they do so.

sentences.zh: 百官執手板，尚書令、僕、尚書，手板頭復有白筆，以紫皮裹之，名曰「笏」。

translations.literal: All officials held hand tablets; for directors and vice directors of the masters of writing and masters of writing, the tablet head also had a white brush wrapped in purple leather—called a "hu."
translations.idiomatic: All officials carried hand tablets; directors and vice directors of the masters of writing and masters of writing had white brushes at the tablet head wrapped in purple leather—called hu.

sentences.zh: 漢末仲長統謂百司皆宜執之。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Zhongchang Tong said all offices should hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Han, Zhongchang Tong argued that every office should carry them.

sentences.zh: 其肩上紫袷囊，名曰「契囊」，世呼爲「紫荷」。

translations.literal: The purple overlapping pouch on the shoulder was called a "qie pouch"; the world called it "purple lotus."
translations.idiomatic: The purple overlapping shoulder pouch was called a qie pouch; common speech named it the "purple lotus."

sentences.zh: 佩玉，自乘輿以下，與晉、宋制同。

translations.literal: Jade pendants—from the imperial vehicle down, the regulations matched Jin and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Jade pendants, from the sovereign down, followed Jin and Song regulations.

sentences.zh: 建元四年，制王公侯卿尹珠水精，其餘用牙蜯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, a regulation fixed that princes, marquises, ministers, and chief administrators used pearl and rock crystal; the rest used ivory and tridacna.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 4 it was ordered that princes, marquises, ministers, and chief administrators use pearl and rock crystal; all others ivory and tridacna.

sentences.zh: 太官宰人服離支衣，後定。

translations.literal: Grand Provision cooks wore lizhi-branch garments; later this was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Provision cooks wore lizhi-branch garments; the rule was later settled.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：文物煌煌，儀品穆穆。

translations.literal: In praise: civil and martial regalia blaze bright; ritual forms stand solemn and still.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: regalia blaze bright; ritual forms stand grave and still.

sentences.zh: 分別禮數，莫過輿服。

translations.literal: To distinguish ritual grades, nothing surpasses carriages and dress.
translations.idiomatic: To mark ritual rank, nothing exceeds carriages and dress.

sentences.zh: 「漆畫牽車」注「戍棟樑」，一本「戍」作「戈」。

translations.literal: On the "lacquer-painted traction carriage," the gloss reads "defense ridgebeam"; in one edition shu is written as ge ("halberd").
translations.idiomatic: On the "lacquer-painted traction carriage," the gloss reads "defense ridgebeam"; one edition reads shu as ge ("halberd").

sentences.zh: 「輿車」注「成校棟樑」，一本「成校」作「戈杖」。

translations.literal: On the "carriage vehicle," the gloss reads "completion-correction ridgebeam"; in one edition cheng-xiao is written as gezhang ("halberd staff").
translations.idiomatic: On the "carriage vehicle," the gloss reads "completion-correction ridgebeam"; one edition reads cheng-xiao as gezhang ("halberd staff").

sentences.zh: 「衣書車」注「刺代棟樑」，「平乘車」注「刺代棟樑」，並疑。

translations.literal: On the "book-and-robe carriage," the gloss reads "pierce-substitute ridgebeam"; on the "level-riding carriage," the gloss reads "pierce-substitute ridgebeam"—both are doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: On the "book-and-robe carriage" and the "level-riding carriage," each gloss reads "pierce-substitute ridgebeam"—both are doubtful.

translations.literal: [1] Endnote marker.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text has used as the base for collation the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi, January 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi (January 1972).
